get.description:
API endpoint to get the available timezones.

This API endpoint retrieves a list of available timezones supported by the system.

API endpoint to get the available countries.

This API endpoint retrieves a list of available countries supported by the system.

List currenciesReturns the catalogue of supported fiat currencies used by the product for forms, validation, and integrations. The response includes a boolean success indicator and a data array of objects.Each object includes code (ISO 4217 alphabetic code) and name (human-readable label). Some entries MAY include an exchange string when the row represents a currency priced or reported against another code (see the application configuration for the authoritative list).The sequence and membership of the catalogue are defined by server configuration and MAY change between releases. Clients SHOULD NOT assume a fixed length.Authorization. The caller MUST authenticate with a valid API key for the tenant (same requirements as other public v1 resources).

API endpoint to get the available nationalities.

This API endpoint retrieves a list of available nationalities supported by the system.

API endpoint to get all available education levels.

This API endpoint retrieves a list of available education levels supported by the system.

API endpoint to get all available employment statuses.

This API endpoint retrieves a list of available employment statuses supported by the system.

API endpoint to get all available relationship types.

This API endpoint retrieves a list of available relationship types supported by the system.

Get system settingsReturns the consolidated system configuration for the authenticated tenant, comprising domain-level and company-level attributes that are exposed through this version of the public HTTP API.The response includes a boolean success indicator and a data object. Property names follow the public v1 contract (for example, language denotes the UI language code, domain denotes the tenant subdomain hostname, and logo_url denotes a signed or public logo URL when configured). The currency field, when present, is the tenant default ISO code; see GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/currencies (List currencies). The login_method property is a JSON array of string slugs; each element MUST be a member of the platform allow list. At the time of publication, the permitted values are: local, google, microsoft, and apple. Additional identifiers MAY be introduced in a future release and are subject to the same validation rules.Further scalar flags (including, where applicable, two_factor_auth, ai_assistant_company_data, and ai_files_summary) are included when relevant to the tenant subscription and configuration. The effective set of properties returned in data is constrained by the caller's authorizations and by tenant-level feature availability.Authorization. The caller MUST possess permission to view domain settings.

post.description:
Update system settingsUpdates permitted domain-level and company-level system attributes for the authenticated tenant. All request payloads are validated prior to persistence; a failed validation results in an error response and no partial update.For the tenant subdomain, the request body MUST use the property name domain. A property named name, if present, is not interpreted for subdomain updates on this route. The property name language MUST match the public GET response contract for the same resource.The login_method property MUST be a JSON array whose elements are string slugs drawn exclusively from the platform allow list. At the time of publication, the permitted values are: local, google, microsoft, and apple. The request MUST NOT supply the internal JSON envelope that nests the array (that pattern is rejected by this API version). Each submitted slug MUST appear at most once; the array denotes the set of methods enabled for the tenant.The currency property is the tenant default ISO currency code (at most three characters); use a code value from GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/currencies (List currencies).Required company-level attributes in the submitted payload include company_name, theme, and currency. Optional company-level attributes include working_days, logo_url or multipart logo, two_factor_auth, ai_assistant_company_data, and ai_files_summary. If the ai-files-summary subscription feature is not enabled for the tenant, a submitted ai_files_summary field MAY be removed from the request prior to validation.Authorization. The caller MUST possess permission to update system settings for each logical field group represented in the submitted payload.

get.description:
List default document folders

This endpoint returns a paginated list of the tenant’s default employee document folders (data.total and data.rows). Requires permission to list default document folders. Query parameter behaviour is described in the Params list; the saved OK (200) example illustrates the response shape.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: (integer) Optional. Pagination offset used together with limit (page-bucket semantics: offset 0 with limit 10 is page 1; offset 10 with limit 10 is page 2). Default when omitted: 0. Non-integer or negative values yield HTTP 422.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: (integer) Optional. Rows per page. Default when omitted: 10. Minimum: 1; maximum: 100 inclusive. Values outside 1–100 yield HTTP 422.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: (string) Optional. Sort field. Allowed: name, created_at, updated_at. Other values are normalized to name.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: (string) Optional. Sort direction. Allowed: asc, desc. Invalid values are normalized to the default for the resource (asc).

post.description:
Create default document folder

Creates a default employee document folder with a display name and role-based permissions for who can view and edit documents in that folder.
Requires permission to create default document folders.
Use List user roles (GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/user-roles) for user_role_id values. Use Get type and permission values (GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/custom-fields-values) for allowed action and condition tokens under data.permission_values.

Request body:

Name
Type
Required
Description
Values

name
string
yes
Folder display name. Maximum 128 characters; must satisfy tenant filename rules and be unique among default folders.
e.g. HR policies

permissions
array
yes
Access rules by user role for folder view and edit. Send as a JSON array (a JSON string is also accepted). Each object: user_role_id (from List user roles), action (view or edit), and condition (string, array of permitted tokens, or null). Allowed action and condition values are in Get type and permission values under data.permission_values. Do not send resource or value in the request body.
e.g. [{"user_role_id":5,"action":"view","condition":"all"},{"user_role_id":5,"action":"edit","condition":["self","manager"]}]

There are no path parameters.

get.description:
Get default document folder

This endpoint returns one default employee document folder, including aggregated permissions rows for folder view/edit by user role (same shape as create and update success payloads). Requires permission to view default document folders. The saved OK (200) example illustrates the response shape.

parameters.name: default_document_folder
parameters.description: (integer) Default document folder id (numeric path segment).

put.description:
Update default document folder

Updates a default employee document folder identified in the path. Replaces the folder display name (when allowed) and the permission matrix for folder view and edit.
Requires permission to update default document folders.
For the system folder with slug employee-home-folder, permission changes are applied; a submitted name is not persisted.
Use List user roles (GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/user-roles) for user_role_id values. Use Get type and permission values (GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/custom-fields-values) for allowed action and condition tokens under data.permission_values.

Request body:

Name
Type
Required
Description
Values

name
string
yes
Folder display name. Maximum 128 characters; must satisfy tenant filename rules and be unique among default folders. Not persisted when the folder slug is employee-home-folder.
e.g. HR policies (revision 2)

permissions
array
yes
Access rules by user role for folder view and edit. Send as a JSON array (a JSON string is also accepted). Each object: user_role_id (from List user roles), action (view or edit), and condition (string, array of permitted tokens, or null). Allowed action and condition values are in Get type and permission values under data.permission_values. Do not send resource or value in the request body.
e.g. [{"user_role_id":5,"action":"view","condition":"all"},{"user_role_id":5,"action":"edit","condition":["self","manager"]}]

Path parameters are documented under Params.

parameters.name: default_document_folder
parameters.description: (integer) Default document folder id.

delete.description:
Delete default document folder

This endpoint removes the default folder identified in the path. On success returns a boolean flag in success. Use the Params list for the optional query flag; Not found (HTTP 404) and Conflict (HTTP 409) examples are illustrative.

parameters.name: default_document_folder
parameters.description: (integer) Default document folder id to delete.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: (integer) Optional. When set to 1, allows deleting a folder that still contains documents. When omitted or 0, the API rejects deletion with HTTP 409 if any documents remain. The Employee Home Folder is never deletable regardless of force.

post.description:
API Endpoint to create an employee.

This API endpoint facilitates the creation of an employee within the system. When creating an employee, it's necessary to provide essential personal information such as first name, last name, and email address. Additionally, the endpoint requires details regarding the employee's hire date, employment status, and manager.
When we are adding a new employee, we should avoid creating loops or circles in the organization hierarchy.
If the is_existing parameter is set to true the onboarding process is bypassed. Otherwise, if it's set to false, the employee is considered a new hire, and the system initiates the onboarding process for the newly hired employee.
In cases where no manager is specified, the employee becomes the head of the company hierarchy.
You can choose to disable the initial system invite.
In case you want to provide some additional information on onboarding new hires at the organization, you should fill in the hire packet object with the necessary information. This allow you to send an a email to the hiring employee containing detailed instructions for their first day of work.

After the successful creation of a newly hired employee's profile, an email is dispatched to the new hire containing essential information required for registering with the domain. This includes details such as login credentials, and any other relevant information to facilitate their smooth integration into the company's systems. Additionally, emails are sent to existing employees who are assigned the responsibility of conducting the onboarding tasks for the new employee.

put.description:
API Endpoint to update the information of an employee.

This API endpoint enables the updating of an employee's information within the system based on the provided employee ID. You can modify various aspects of an employee's record, including personal details, contact information, designation, and any other relevant data stored within the system.

When updating an employee's profile, you can modify the custom fields associated with that employee. However, it is important to note that the availability of this feature is dependent on your TalentHR subscription (Refer to the Introductory chapter for further details). The custom fields associated with an employee can be retrieved using the 'Get employee's custom fields' endpoint.

delete.description:
API Endpoint to delete the specified employee.

This API endpoint facilitates the deletion of a specified employee from the system based on the provided employee ID. Upon invoking this endpoint, the system permanently removes the employee's record, along with all associated information and data stored within the system. It triggers a cascading effect that removes all associated records and data related to that employee. This includes various items such as job records, employment status, performance, review, assets,benefits information, personal documents, task assignments and any other information tied directly to the employee's profile.
Before deleting the employee, the system checks if any other employees report to him/her directly. If there are, these subordinate employees are automatically reassigned to a new manager. Typically, the new manager is the supervisor of the deleted employee. This ensures that there is no disruption in the workflow and that the responsibilities of the deleted employee are seamlessly redistributed within the organization.
Warning: If the employee being deleted is the head of the company, meaning they have no manager above them in the organizational hierarchy, the deletion cannot proceed.
Note: Once an employee is deleted, their email address can be used on your domain again.

post.description:
API Endpoint to terminate the employment of an employee.

This API endpoint demonstrates the process of employee terminations within the HR system by incorporating the effective date of termination and the reason for termination. Users can remain active and utilize the system normally until the final termination date is specified. Upon the termination process, the system automatically assigns offboarding tasks to relevant users, ensuring a seamless transition for the terminated employee (employees are being notified also via email). If the termination date matches the current date, the user is instantly terminated, preventing further access to the system.
When an employee is terminated, the system initiates several automatic procedures to ensure a smooth transition and maintain organizational integrity. Upon the employee's termination, employees who are under his/her supervision are reassigned to the manager of the terminated employee. Concurrently, any incomplete task assignments of the terminated employee are transferred to this manager as well.
Furthermore, the system automatically deletes any job records, compensation records, manager records, or employment status records that are dated after the termination. Additionally, any time off requests(rejected or remain unanswered) from the terminated employee will be removed. Finally, if the terminated employee is part of a hiring team for a job position, he/she will be removed from the hiring team as part of the termination process.
Note: The information of the terminated user remains within the system after the termination.

Rehire a terminated employee

This endpoint rehires an employee identified by the path id after a prior termination. It restores employment records, reporting line, optional job and compensation payloads, and workflows equivalent to the in-product rehire flow. Requires permission to hire employees.

Preconditions

The employee identified in the path must currently be terminated.
reports_to_employee_id is required — unlike hire, omitting manager is not supported for this flow.
hire_date (YYYY-MM-DD) must validate as strictly after the latest termination effective date.

Request body
For Content-Type: application/json, send employment_status and optional job_record, compensation_record as nested objects in the payload (parallel to Create an employee (Hire)).

Type
Required
Description

string
yes

yes

object

e.g. false

API Endpoint to update an employee's combined Time Off budget.
This endpoint sets a combined entitlement target for the employee, time-off type, and cycle identified by the fixed time-off budget id in the path.
new_budget is the target total of:

fixed original_budget, plus
accrued entitlement (accrual_original_budget), plus
carry-on entitlement (accrual_carry_on_original_budget).

Increase (new_budget above the current combined total): the entire increase is applied to the fixed original budget only. Accrual balances are not increased through this endpoint.

Accrual entitlement can only be decreased via this endpoint (never increased).

API Endpoint to book a time off request.
This endpoint facilitates the booking of a time-off request for the specified employee. A time off request is an entity that describes the decision making process for approving time off.It can be used for various reasons such as vacation, personal matters, bereavement or illness.
The request body includes the start and end dates for the time-off request, the type of time-off requested, the preapproved attribute indicating whether the request will be automatically approved or requires manager approval, the amount option providing a detailed analysis of each day's duration (e.g., full-day as 1, half-day as 0.5, etc), and can include hours in the per-day breakdown when hour-based amounts apply, optional notes accompanying the request, and an optional file attachment for supporting documents (sent as the multipart attachment part when used; see the request body table for size and type rules).

For future-hire employees, the time-off request cannot have a start date before their hire date.
For terminated employees, the time-off request must come before the termination date.

Note: The start_date and end_date must fall within one year from the current date.

When the "book time off" request is successfully submitted and preapproved is false or the part is omitted, an email is automatically dispatched to the employee's manager, requesting approval or rejection of the time off request. This endpoint allows you to fetch a list of valid filters for the directory. Utilize the 'id' field from the returned objects to filter employees in the 'directory' endpoint.

API Endpoint to retrieve all the employees with some information for each of them.
This endpoint retrieves comprehensive information regarding the system's employee directory.
You can paginate results using limit and offset. If limit is omitted, it defaults to 10. The maximum supported value for limit is 100. If offset is omitted, it defaults to 0.
In addition to pagination parameters, you can utilize filters to precisely retrieve the data you want. You can find suitable IDs for the current filters by accessing the 'directory filters' endpoint.
Optionally, you can request employee custom fields to be included in the response by providing the custom_fields query parameter as a comma-separated list of field slugs (from GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/custom-fields). Standard/predefined field slugs are merged at the root of each row, while custom (non-predefined) field slugs are returned under the custom_fields array.

parameters.description: The maximum number of rows to return per request. Defaults to 10 and can be set up to 100.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: (integer) Optional. Pagination offset used together with limit (page-bucket semantics: offset 0 with limit 10 is page 1; offset 10 with limit 10 is page 2). Default when omitted: 0.

parameters.description: Filters for the directory arrays with their Ids (integer), ('location' => [],'department' => [],'division' => [],'time_off' => [],'time_off_type' => [],'emp_state' => [],'time_off_status' => []). Example: location=36;emp_state=1,2,3,5;

parameters.description:
Comma-separated employee custom field slugs to include in each row. You can include slugs for standard/predefined fields and custom (non-predefined) fields as returned by GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/custom-fields.
When provided:

Standard/predefined fields are merged at the root of each rows[] item (e.g., address, city, postal_code, country, sec_address, etc.).

API Endpoint to retrieve all the current employees with their managers.
This endpoint retrieves comprehensive information regarding the system's organization chart.
The organization chart shows the company's internal structure by detailing the roles, and relationships between the employees of the company.

API Endpoint to retrieve the available filters for calendar.
This endpoint allows you to fetch a list of valid filters for the system's calendar. Utilize the 'id' field from the returned objects to filter employees in the 'calendar' endpoint.

API Endpoint to retrieve the dates that each employee(s) is off, for the specified date range.
This endpoint retrieves comprehensive information regarding the system's calendar.
The calendar endpoint provides information about employee time off and holidays. Users can filter this information based on various criteria, including pending time-offs, completed time-offs, time-offs for specific divisions, departments, locations, time off types, and employment statuses. Additionally, historical data of time-offs for terminated employees are also available. Besides the filters, you have the option to provide the employee_id parameter to the calendar endpoint. This allows you to specify the employee of your choice and retrieve his/her calendar data.
Note: If the end date is not provided, the calendar period will extend from the start date provided to the end of the month in which the start date falls.

You have the option to utilize filters to precisely retrieve the data you want. You can find suitable IDs for the current filters by accessing the 'directory filters' endpoint. The filters include information regarding time off status, location, division, departments, employment status, and time off types.
Note: Filter options in the filters are represented as arrays of IDs. However, the time off status (as time_off in filters) for the calendar has two options and they are represented as strings: "pending" and "approved". These can be specified directly in the filters. (E.g. time_off=pending,approved;)
Note: If no filter provided then the calendar will return all the employees (included the terminated) with their time-offs and the holidays for the specified period.

API Endpoint to change the status of the specified asset.
This endpoint allows for the modification of an asset's status, applicable to both inventory and membership assets, with each type having its distinct set of statuses.
For membership assets, there are only two possible statuses:

Available: Indicates the asset is ready and accessible for use.
Retired: Signifies that the asset is no longer in service or use.

Inventory assets, on the other hand, have a broader range of five possible statuses:

Available: The asset is not currently being used and is ready for deployment.
In Use: Indicates the asset is actively being utilized.
In Service: The asset is undergoing maintenance or repairs.
Broken: The asset is damaged and not in working condition.
Retired: Similar to the membership asset, this status means the asset is no longer in service.

For inventory assets with an assigned user, the transition to the "In Use" status is specifically relevant when the asset is moving from a "Broken" or "In Service" status. It is important to note that once an inventory asset is marked as "Retired," any association with an assigned user is removed, effectively preventing any further transition to the "In Use" status.

For an inventory asset with an assigned user, transitioning to the "in-use" status is applicable primarily when the current status is "broken" or "in-service". post.description:
API Endpoint to set compensation band ranges.
This endpoint replaces the tenant’s compensation band definitions used by compensation reports. Compensation bands partition annual compensation into contiguous ranges; each band uses a lower bound (from) and an optional upper bound (to) in the tenant’s compensation currency units.
Requires permission to set compensation reports (not merely view).

Every band except the last must include non-null from and to; from must be strictly less than to.
The last band may set to to null for an open upper bound; when to is present on the last band, from must be strictly less than to.
Each from and to may be a JSON number or a numeric string (integer or decimal).

On success, the response includes the persisted bands under data.ranges.

Request body:

Name
Type
Required
Description
Values

compensation_ranges
array or string
yes
Ordered list of compensation bands for the tenant. Send as a JSON array (canonical) or as a JSON string that decodes to the same array structure. Each element is an object with from and optional to. Every band except the last must include non-null from and to; from must be strictly less than to. The last band may set to to null for an open upper bound; when to is present on the last band, from must be strictly less than to. Each from and to may be a JSON number or a numeric string (integer or decimal).
e.g. [{"from":0,"to":50000},{"from":50000,"to":120000},{"from":120000,"to":null}]

This endpoint returns company-level performance review aggregates (value and work question categories) for the selected cycles.
Requires permission to view performance reports. The tenant subscription must have the Performance Review feature enabled.
Provide either a period preset, a start_date/end_date pair, or target cycles via actual_review_cycles as described in the Params list.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: (string) Conditionally required. Use l12m or l6m for a rolling window when start_date / end_date are not used. Send start_date and end_date together when period is omitted (unless actual_review_cycles selects cycles instead). Other values fail validation (HTTP 422).

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: (string, date) Conditionally required with end_date when period is omitted. Format YYYY-MM-DD. Together with end_date, the range must not exceed 36 months.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: (string, date) Conditionally required with start_date when period is omitted. Format YYYY-MM-DD, must be on or after start_date.

parameters.name: actual_review_cycles
parameters.description: (string) Optional. Comma-separated performance review cycle ids. When present, the server uses only those cycles (unknown ids are ignored). Period and custom date rules are not applied for validation in that mode.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: (string) Optional. Breakdown dimension. Allowed: location, department, division, gender, age, seniority. Other values fail validation (HTTP 422). When omitted, the response uses overall totals per answer.

get.description:
This endpoint returns summarized approved, non-cancelled time off for the resolved reporting window, including monthly totals by leave type and working-weekday totals and percentage shares by type.
Requires permission to view time off reports.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: (string) Conditionally required. Allowed: l12m, the current calendar year, or the previous calendar year (four-digit year, e.g. 2026). Omit when using start_date and end_date together.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: (string, date) Conditionally required with end_date when period is omitted. YYYY-MM-DD, not after the end of the current calendar month.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: (string, date) Conditionally required with start_date when period is omitted. YYYY-MM-DD, on or after start_date. Maximum span with start_date is 36 months.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: (string) Optional. Semicolon-separated key=value pairs for location, department, and division only (numeric ids), e.g. location=5;department=3. Retrieve available values via GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/reports/filters with model=timeoff_budgets_report.

get.description:

Requires permission to view time tracking reports and the Time Tracking subscription feature.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: (string) Conditionally required. Allowed: l12m, the current calendar year, or the previous calendar year (four-digit year). Omit when using start_date and end_date together.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: (string, date) Conditionally required with end_date when period is omitted. YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: (string, date) Conditionally required with start_date when period is omitted. YYYY-MM-DD, on or after start_date. Maximum span is 36 months.

parameters.name: filter

parameters.name: group_by

get.description:
This endpoint returns employees with tracked minutes in the resolved window, broken down by selected tags and a running total.
Requires permission to view time tracking reports and the Time Tracking subscription feature. Preset period values are interpreted in the authenticated user’s timezone.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: (string) Conditionally required. Allowed: today, yesterday, week, month, or omit when using start_date and end_date (YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: (string, date) Conditionally required with end_date when period is omitted. YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: (string, date) Conditionally required with start_date when period is omitted. YYYY-MM-DD, on or after start_date. Maximum span is 36 months.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: (string) Optional. Semicolon-separated key=value pairs (for example location, department, division, job title, employment status, manager, gender, tag). Retrieve available values via GET https://pubapi.talenthr.io/v1/reports/filters with model=employee_time_tracking_report using the same period / start_date / end_date.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: (string) Optional. Comma-separated time tracking tag ids to include. Include the token na to count minutes logged without a tag.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: (string) Optional. Filters by employee name fragments and related directory fields (server-side matching).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: (string) Optional. total (default when sort is omitted), name, na (untagged minutes), or a numeric time tracking tag id. order defaults to desc when omitted.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: (string) Optional. asc or desc.
